variants.headline: Shipbuilding for the colony route
variants.sub: Shipbuilding by the home world has provided a larger vessel or another vessel for the colony route.
variants.body:
The home world has built a larger ship or an additional ship for the colony route. The construction is a transport development, not an announcement of arrival. In assessing {target}, readers should distinguish provision of a vessel from an unreported schedule, cargo or immediate change in supplies.

A ship has been built for the route. Good material for a grand picture of the future; less useful as proof of what is on a shop shelf today. Keep the distinction clear. Building a vessel and watching it arrive are different stories, however attractive it is to combine them.

We remain critical of {target}. A shipbuilding development should not place transport stewardship beyond scrutiny; the colony deserves a demanding standard rather than automatic admiration for the announcement of a vessel. Readers deserve a clear story and a straight answer about responsibility.
